title: 1972 AHSME Problem 22
statement: If \(a\pm bi\) \((b\ne0)\) are imaginary roots of the equation \(x^3+qx+r=0,\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) \(q,\) and \(r\) are real numbers, then \(q\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\) is:

solutions.text:
The conjugate root is \(a-bi.\) Since the sum of the three roots is \(0,\) the third root is \(-2a.\) By Vieta’s formulas, \[ \begin{aligned} q&=(a+bi)(a-bi)\\ &\quad-2a(a+bi)\\ &\quad-2a(a-bi)\\ &=a^2+b^2-4a^2\\ &=b^2-3a^2. \end{aligned} \]

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Because the \(x^2\) coefficient is zero, determine the third root and then use the sum of pairwise products
